status: ROOT MATHEMATICAL ACCEPTANCE after complete frozen source and independent audit read, with analytic reconstruction
accepted_scope: For a symmetric zero-diagonal M with nonzero hafnian and actual MC=tau I, every actual cofactor row has support size one or at least three; size one is equivalent to membership in an isolated M edge.
In a full ternary source at n>=6, a vertex nonmatching in B or C has at least four sites at H-distance greater than two. A 3-connected B/C support union makes this true at every vertex.

Every H graph has at least six vertices with four far sites and at least n+6 unordered far pairs. A fixed color's cofactor row is supported in the intersection of the far sets for the other two colors.
If B and C have isolated edges p-q and p-r, their distinct partners q,r are nonadjacent in every color, by the full ternary routing rectangle theorem.

A girth-at-least-five nonmatching component of minimum degree delta requires n>=delta^2+5, rounded to the next even integer. Under complementary pair 3-connectivity, every vertex of a cubic component at n=12 belongs to at least two distinct four-cycles.
root_reconstruction: For a two-entry cofactor row a=C[p,q], b=C[p,r], sum the off-diagonal CM row against the common residual hafnians K_w. The actual expansions give 0=ab+ba, contradicting ab!=0 over C.

A nonmatching B vertex has at least three nonzero actual B cofactor entries, all H-far. The private C partner is also H-far and its original mixed two-site coefficient kills the B cofactor there, giving a fourth distinct site.

For isolated complementary edges, the odd-routing residual support sets are the singleton partners. The four-site H hafnian then reduces to H[p,u]H[q,r], forcing H[q,r]=0; the other two colors vanish at q,r by isolation.

A girth-five component has a radius-two ball of at least 1+delta^2 at every vertex. If n<=delta^2+4, all those vertices would be matching in B and C, leaving at most three exterior sites for a required nonmatching component.
not_established: That the cofactor matrix itself satisfies an actual scalar inverse-cofactor identity
That every vertex has four far sites without the local nonmatching or pair-connectivity premise
General n=12 exclusion, existential weighted four-deletion, or conjecture closure
